# Summary of Cairn System Rules

## Pulses
A pulse grows a cairn's height. The growth amount equals the stride plus a bonus equal to the number of complete strides already contained in the current height. Taller cairns grow more per pulse because they contain more complete strides. You calculate complete strides by integer division (rounding down).

## Repeated Pulses
When applying multiple pulses in sequence, you must recalculate the complete strides fresh at each step using the updated height. You cannot reuse the stride count from earlier pulses—the height changes, so the stride count changes.

## Leaks
A leak removes marks after a pulse happens. The number of marks lost equals the pulsed height divided by the leak size (rounded down). The leak is applied to the height after the pulse, not before. This reduces growth but doesn't necessarily stop it.

## Draining Cycles
Draining combines pulses with fixed losses. Each cycle applies one pulse, then removes a fixed drain amount. The cairn empties when the drain outpaces the pulse growth. The process is iterative—you must cycle through each step because the pulse amount changes as height changes.

## Finding Origins (Working Backwards)
To find a starting height given a final height after multiple pulses, reverse each pulse one at a time. Test values to find which height before the pulse would produce the observed height after. Work backwards through all pulses sequentially.

## Merging Cairns
Merging combines two cairns using weighted shares. Calculate a fractional portion of each cairn's height (rounded down), add them together, then add a tether bonus based on the shorter cairn's size. The tether is multiplied by the complete tens in the shorter cairn's height.
